readmeExcerpt: # e2e [e2e](https://e2e.com?utm_source=e2e&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme_intro) is an end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps. Describe a goal in natural language and an agent drives the app to reach it. Check the result with locators and assertions in the same test. ```ts // tests/checkout.e2e.ts import { test, expect } from 'e2e'; test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/settings/billing'); await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan'); await agent.assert('the invoice preview shows a prorated amount'); await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro'); }); ``` An agent step that a later assertion verifies records its actions, and the next run replays them with no model calls until the app changes. Tests without agent steps need no model. Bring your own subscription, API key, or local model. ## Quick start ```bash npx e2e init ``` `init` asks for an engine, web or mobile, and a model provider, then writes a config and an example test. The [quickstart](https://e2e.com/docs/quickstart) covers the rest. To see a finished setup in your stack, open [`examples/`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/tree/main/examples): Vite, Next.js, Astro, Angular, Expo, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin Multiplatform, readmeHtml:
e2e

e2e is an end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps. Describe a goal in natural language and an agent drives the app to reach it. Check the result with locators and assertions in the same test.

// tests/checkout.e2e.ts
import { test, expect } from 'e2e';

test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => {
  await app.open('/settings/billing');

  await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan');
  await agent.assert('the invoice preview shows a prorated amount');

  await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro');
});

An agent step that a later assertion verifies records its actions, and the next run replays them with no model calls until the app changes. Tests without agent steps need no model. Bring your own subscription, API key, or local model.

Quick start

npx e2e init

init asks for an engine, web or mobile, and a model provider, then writes a config and an example test. The quickstart covers the rest.

To see a finished setup in your stack, open examples/: Vite, Next.js, Astro, Angular, Expo, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Kotlin Multiplatform, Flutter, and .NET MAUI, each a standalone project with a passing suite.

Packages

Core

Package What it does
e2e The SDK, runner, and CLI.
@e2e-dev/web Browser engine: Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through Playwright.
@e2e-dev/mobile iOS and Android engine: simulators and emulators through agent-device.
@e2e-dev/decision Decision-model executors for bounded semantic actions and assertions, and decisionFilter(), which leaves out the tests a pull request is unlikely to affect.
@e2e-dev/acp Runs agent steps on your own coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) over the Agent Client Protocol.

Integrations

Package What it does
@e2e-dev/kernel Kernel hosted browsers for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/lightpanda Lightpanda, the open-source headless browser, started per run for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/smol smol machines browsers for the web engine: by default, each attempt branches a warm Chromium microVM.
@e2e-dev/testmu TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) hosted Android emulators, iOS simulators, and real devices for the mobile engine, and hosted Chrome and Edge for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/e2b E2B sandboxes: Android 16 for the mobile engine, and Chromium for the web engine.
@e2e-dev/browserstack BrowserStack App Automate real Android and iOS devices for the mobile engine.
@e2e-dev/limrun Limrun hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for mobile tests.
@e2e-dev/eas Expo Simulators hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators for the mobile engine.
@e2e-dev/github Reporter that posts results as a pull request comment.
@e2e-dev/html-reporter Reporter that writes the run as one HTML page, with steps, screenshots, and video.

Community

See Community packages for third-party integrations and how to add yours.

Documentation

e2e.com/docs. The e2e package ships every page, so coding agents can read them offline in node_modules/e2e/docs.

Join us

Join us in changing how software gets tested. We are hiring.

Questions? Ask on Discord. Issues are for bugs and feature requests.

Want to hack on e2e? See Contributing. We prefer an issue or a Discord discussion before a pull request.

Security

Please don't open public issues for security vulnerabilities. Follow SECURITY.md and report them to security@e2e.com.

Telemetry

The CLI sends anonymous usage data, such as which commands and engines run and where runs fail, but no test content, app content, or credentials. Opt out with npx e2e telemetry disable or E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. Telemetry lists every field.

Status

Note

e2e is in active development on the way to 1.0. APIs and config can still change between minor releases.

- [#1552](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1552) [`d2556bc`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d2556bc23fd01afe8f72a2e94e5fc18b4787b433) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - **Breaking:** `inputValue()` on a node with no value, such as a heading or a button, and `isChecked()` on a node with no checked state throw `ACTION_FAILED`, as in Playwright, instead of returning `""` and `false`. releases.name: @e2e-dev/web@0.15.5
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- [#1479](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1479) [`d15a98e`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/d15a98e0711a185873a7a57a108dd254673e327c) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `app.baseUrl` no longer ends in a slash, so `${app.baseUrl}/api/users` requests `/api/users` instead of `//api/users`. With `test` from `@e2e-dev/web`, `app.baseUrl` is typed `string`, since a `web()` target always declares `app.url`. A test that relied on the trailing slash, such as `${app.baseUrl}api/users` or `new URL('users', app.baseUrl)` on a URL with a path, adds the slash itself.

- [#1553](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/pull/1553) [`9267248`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/commit/9267248c4c45716f87bda581563023c9c6b4a067) Thanks [@okwasniewski](https://github.com/okwasniewski)! - `browser.evaluate` returns its result when the evaluated code deletes or replaces page globals such as `Map` or `Object`, and on pages that delete `Array` or `JSON`. aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source AI testing framework built on Playwright for generating and executing end-to-end tests.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: e2e is an AI-native testing framework that automates the creation and execution of end-to-end web and mobile tests. It leverages Playwright under the hood to interact with applications while using large language models to dynamically generate test scripts based on natural language descriptions. The system can interpret user flows, generate the necessary assertions, and execute them across different browser environments. By integrating AI into the testing pipeline, it reduces the manual maintenance overhead typically associated with brittle test selectors.
keyFeatures: AI Test Generation: Translates plain English descriptions of user flows into executable Playwright test code.
Playwright Foundation: Built on top of the robust Playwright engine for reliable cross-browser automation.
Self-Healing Selectors: Uses AI to dynamically identify UI elements, reducing failures when DOM structures change.
Cross-Platform Testing: Supports automated testing across both web applications and mobile web environments.
Framework Agnostic: Tests the rendered application independently of the underlying frontend framework.

useCases.title: Automated Regression Testing
useCases.description: Continuously verify that critical user journeys remain functional after code deployments.

useCases.title: Test Suite Bootstrapping
useCases.description: Rapidly generate a baseline suite of end-to-end tests for a legacy application without existing coverage.

useCases.title: Non-Technical QA Automation
useCases.description: Allow product managers and QA analysts to write functional tests using natural language.

useCases.title: Cross-Browser Verification
useCases.description: Ensure consistent application behavior across Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox engines.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: QA engineers, software developers in test (SDETs), and full-stack developers looking to modernize their testing infrastructure. Users should be familiar with end-to-end testing concepts and Node.js environments.
